extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and research-integrity professionals interested in publication ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and evaluating improper image practices and related data-availability problems in biomedical research papers (e.g., western blots, microscopy) that can warrant correction or retraction. Focuses on detectable manipulations, duplicated/rotated reuse, and inability to produce original data.

rubrics_metrics.name: grayscale inversion used to misrepresent image type
rubrics_metrics.description: The grayscale of a PCR gel image was inverted and the consequent image was used to represent Western blot data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In Figure 1B the β-tubulin Western blot panels were generated from the GAPDH PCR image (Figure 1A) by inverting grayscale. In Figure 2 each PCR image in panel A was reversed and adjusted for contrast/black level to represent western blot images in panel B. In Figure 6A and 6B similar grayscale reversals and adjustments were used to create β-tubulin and MMP-3 blot panels. Such inversion and re-use of an image to represent a different assay/type of data is an integrity breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: image splicing (visible seams/lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical lines suggestive of image splicing were observed in panels, indicating possible assembly from multiple sources or manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In Figure 6A vertical lines were seen in the 1st, 4th, 5th, and 7th panels (MMP-3/iPS, GAPDH/B6G-2, MMP-3/E14Tg2a, MMP-3/KN-3). Visible seams or lines are a warning sign that lanes or regions may have been stitched together and should be explained with original source data.

rubrics_metrics.name: reuse/duplication of the same image (including rotated reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: The same image was used in multiple panels, sometimes with rotation (e.g., the 6th panel rotated 180° relative to the 2nd panel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In Figure 6A the same image appears in the 2nd and 6th panels (GAPDH/iPS, GAPDH/E14Tg2a) with the 6th rotated 180 degrees. Reuse of an identical image to represent different samples/conditions (even if rotated) is inappropriate unless explicitly declared and justified with source data.

rubrics_metrics.name: duplicate data presented across experiments with adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Image regions (e.g., lanes) appear duplicated across panels representing different experiments, with adjustments such as contrast/brightness changes and vertical enlargement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The first four lanes in the 1st and 7th panels (MMP-3/iPS and MMP-3/KN-3) appear to present duplicate data; the image in the 1st panel was adjusted for contrast/brightness and vertically enlarged relative to the 7th. Duplicating lanes or images across experiments and altering them to appear different undermines result validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: brightness/contrast adjustments that prevent verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Brightness and contrast settings on western blot figures do not allow confirmation of the integrity of the results as presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Editors noted that the brightness and contrast on western blot figures in the 2015 paper prevented confirmation of image integrity. Excessive/obscuring adjustments make it impossible to verify bands and require original, unprocessed images for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: repeated/similar control blots across panels (possible reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control blots (e.g., β-tubulin) appear similar across different panels, suggesting possible reuse rather than independent controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The β-tubulin blots appear similar in Fig 7 panels A & D, B & E, and C & F. Reuse of loading-control or housekeeping blots across distinct experiments is suspect unless explicitly documented and justified with raw data showing the same blot was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: reuse/duplication of microscopy images across different experiments/figures
rubrics_metrics.description: BrdU and apoptosis microscopy images in multiple figures/panels appear to report the same data despite representing different experiments or conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BrdU and apoptosis images in Fig 4B, Fig 5B, and Fig 6B for experiments i, ii, iii appear the same; BrdU images in panel vi of Fig 4B and 6B represent different experiments but look identical; apoptosis images in panel vi of Fig 4B, Fig 5B, and Fig 6B appear identical. Identical microscopy images used to represent different experiments are a red flag and require original image files with metadata for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: original/underlying data not available
rubrics_metrics.description: The original data underlying the reported results are not available; authors were unable to provide clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both notices state that the underlying/raw data supporting the results are not available; the investigating committee tentatively confirmed concerns about image quality and loss of original data. Lack of raw data prevents verification and is a primary reason for retraction when image issues are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: editorial retraction when integrity concerns and institutional recommendation exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors will retract an article in light of integrity concerns and in line with the institution’s recommendation when image manipulation and missing data undermine the validity of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: PLOS ONE Editors retracted both articles after the university investigation confirmed concerns and the underlying data were unavailable. Editorial action considers both the nature of the manipulation and the availability of original data and institutional findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: author response/consent status documented
rubrics_metrics.description: Author agreement or lack of response to retraction decisions is recorded and considered part of the post-publication process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The notices list which authors agreed with the retraction and which did not respond or could not be reached (e.g., NO, MM, HY, RK, KN, AK, HN agreed; TH did not respond). Documenting author responses is standard practice in retraction notices and can inform transparency about disputes.
